thread:
alex: FYI we got a support ticket from Acme — customer hits 403 when switching projects in the console after SSO + MFA.

alex: Repro steps they sent:
1) Login via Okta SSO (MFA challenge passes)
2) Click org -> project switch
3) Console shows a 403 page and action buttons are disabled

alex: They say API calls with their API key still return data but console actions fail.

maria: @alex can you paste the network response and the session cookie headers? need org id too.

alex: Org id: org_98765. Network snippet from browser devtools:

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-request-id: r2k-33
set-cookie: session=eyJ...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
x-auth-source: okta-sso
x-session-mfa: required
```

samir: Heads up — we deployed an IDP claim normalization change recently. deploy-bot shows:

deploy-bot: idp-claims/normalize v3 deployed to prod @ 1763141700

samir: My suspicion: our authz layer is expecting an explicit `mfa:true` claim but Okta is returning `amr": ["pwd","otp"]`. Claim name mismatch means console never grants elevated console scopes.

katie: Customer screenshot also shows project list present but all "Actions" buttons greyed out. Can someone introspect their session token? Suggest running:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SESSION" https://api.redwood.example/v1/auth/introspect
```

maria: I introspected the token they provided. Introspect output (redacted): scopes: `read:projects` (no `write:projects`, no `console:actions`) and claims include `amr: [\"pwd\",\"otp\"]`. Our policy currently checks `mfa: true` claim because of normalize v3.

alex: Customer needs a quick workaround. I proposed issuing a short-lived service token with `write:projects` scope so they can continue ops while we patch claim handling.

samir: I'll implement a fallback in authz: treat presence of `amr` containing `otp` or `mfa` as equivalent to `mfa:true`. Pushing a small canary now.

deploy-bot: rollout idp-claims/fallback-amr -> canary @ 1763141810

maria: OK noted. I've updated the ticket with repro steps, introspect output, and the temporary service-token workaround for Acme.

alex: Thanks team — will follow up with customer after canary confirms. :thumbsup:

samir: If canary looks good I'll promote to prod and add an integration test for both `mfa:true` and `amr`-based detection to prevent regression.

maria: keeping this open until prod promotion.
